summary:
ORION: Vital Intelligence is a health monitoring dashboard created by Project TIAD. V.I.T.A.L. (Virtual Telemetry for Astronaut Life-support). This system helps NASA's flight surgeons to keep track of astronaut's health and stats during space missions.

Using  telemetry from the ARTEMIS VII crew ORION monitors important health signs. These stats will include heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen levels (aka SpO2) core temperature, sleeping patterns, hydration and even radiation exposure. Every data point is checked against safety standards which are set by The NASA Human Research Program (aka HRP). Based on the readings astronauts are placed into 1/3 categories, +healthy+, !warning!, !!critical!!

This classification makes it easy for the NASA flight surgeons to notice problems efficiently and easily. Issues like oxygen, high fevers or sudden radiation spikes can be seen and acted on immediately, instead of wasting crucial and valuable time.

We have also added an SI Assistant into the console. This feature lets flight surgeons ask questions. They get answers and medical protocol guidance based on current crew data.

We have also added a authorization system so that only the people with the info can log in and view valuable and crucial data.

As astronauts move from Earth to the Moon and Mars, communication delays grow longer. ORION helps flight surgeons stay ahead of health risks. It gives them clearer information. This means protection, for the crew during deep space travel.
details:
Created by Project TIAD- V.I.T.A.L (Virtual telemetry for Astronaut Life-support), ORION: Vital intelligence ( Orbital Response and integrated Operator Network) is a mission control web-based dashboard which is made for NASA flight surgeons to monitor astronaut's health and stats in real time.

Using biometric sensor data from the ARTEMIS VII crew, ORION tracks around 10 vital measurements for each astronaut's wellbeing, such as it being: heart rate, systolic and diastolic blood pressure, blood oxygen (SpO₂), respiratory rate, core body temperature, heart rate variability (HRV), sleep hours, cumulative radiation (mSv), and also hydration percentages.

We also had to consider many factors while building this project, such as bug fixes, practicality, creativity, visuals, and other things that may have been brushed off otherwise, which would've otherwise lead to failure and poorly coordinated if not for the critical-thinking used and the factors applied.

Instead of making flight surgeons scan raw spreadsheets which is inefficient and time taking during crucial times, ORION compares every vital sign against NASA Human Research Program (HRP) reference bands and automatically sorts crew members into Nominal, Warning, or Critical status. Any astronaut with a dangerous reading, such as low oxygen (88% SpO₂) or high fever (38.6 °C) paired with above average radiation levels (168 mSv)is flagged at the top of the Attention Queue.

Our project is creative as we have used many tools, brainstormed ideas, and have communicated efficiently, while also reminding ourselves that we have come here to learn and explore new fields of education, and explore the world of code.

Flight surgeons can click any crew card to inspect historical trend charts, review medical officer notes, and log new manual vital sweeps during a shift, to ensure deep research of the health and wellbeing of our hardworking and valuable astronauts.

Our built-in Situational Intelligence (SI) Assistant lets flight surgeons ask questions in English like ( "Who needs attention first this shift?") and immediately returns protocol guidance based on live crew data which it learned to grasp and understand under many attempts of previous prototypes of RNG-based Data.

Our team has used JavaScript (JSX), HTML5, CSS3, and TOML as our main coding languages for this project.
